The people of Hadhramaut, the long valley of eastern Yemen, have for centuries left home in large numbers for the lands of the Indian Ocean. The great wave came in the 1700s and 1800s.

Hadhramis settled in Java, Singapore, the Malay states, Hyderabad, Gujarat and East Africa. They were traders, soldiers, landlords and religious teachers. Families of sayyids, descendants of the Prophet from towns such as Tarim, became leading Muslim scholars in Southeast Asia and helped shape Islam there.

Money sent home paid for the palaces of Tarim and Seiyun and kept up towns such as Shibam. Many Arab Indonesians and Malaysians, and many leading Saudi business families, trace their roots to Hadhramaut.
